clue.text: Explain where the lost dog came from

definitions.meaning: to set out a matter in detail, clarifying it

definitions.text: where the lost dog came from
definitions.meaning: a rescued stray is a former inmate of the dog pound

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to account for the origins of a stray dog.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a pun: split the word as EX (former) and POUND (the compound for stray dogs).
explanation.definitionFit: To expound a theory is to set it out and interpret it in detail, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Right in but it's taken out

indicators.note: Right is placed in the middle of the word for but

parts.note: but, as in everyone but me, means except

explanation.surface: A puzzling claim that something is both inside and removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts R inside EXCEPT. The definition reads as a whole phrase: an extract is something that is taken out of a longer text.
explanation.definitionFit: An excerpt is a passage lifted from a book or film, so it is a thing taken out.

clue.text: Correct to hold son is to succeed

indicators.note: the word for correct grips the son inside it

parts.note: correct, as in correct behaviour, means proper
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Advice that behaving properly towards a son leads to success.
explanation.definitionFit: To prosper is to thrive or do well, a plain synonym of succeeding.

clue.text: Commanded by junior

definitions.meaning: a soldier serving ... a general is commanded by that general
an ...-secretary or ...-manager is junior in rank

explanation.definitionFit: Being under someone means subordinate to them, both commanded by them and junior to them.

clue.text: Target area for local missile launchers

definitions.text: Target area for local missile launchers

parts.words: Target area for local missile launchers
parts.note: sounds military, but the local is the pub and the missiles are darts thrown by its players

explanation.surface: A military briefing about a target for nearby rocket launchers.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the local' is one's neighbourhood pub, where darts is a traditional game.
explanation.definitionFit: The circular board in a pub is the target the darts players aim their small missiles at.

clue.text: The mace in a form still used as a weapon

indicators.note: the letters are reshaped into a new form

explanation.surface: A remark that the mace, in some version, remains a weapon today.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a form' rearranges the letters of THE MACE; 'still used as a' joins the anagram to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A machete is a broad-bladed chopping knife that can be wielded as a weapon.

clue.text: Ecclesiastical residence for chap from the home counties

parts.note: a chap is a man
the home counties are the counties around London, in the south-east of England, SE

explanation.surface: A vicarage is described as home to a man from near London.
explanation.walkthrough: The home counties are the English counties that surround London, so they stand for SE, south-east.
explanation.definitionFit: A manse is the house provided for a minister, especially in Scotland, so a church residence.

clue.text: Check study on stress

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn
stress and strain are synonyms

explanation.surface: Advice to examine a study for signs of stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' links the pieces, one placed on top of the other in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrain is to restrain or hold back, which is one sense of to check.

clue.text: Dead to the world

parts.note: the idiom means fast asleep, but read literally it means gone from the earth for good

explanation.definitionFit: A species that has died out completely is gone from the whole world.

clue.text: His choice will get cross

parts.note: sounds like someone sulking, but a voter marks a cross by the candidate chosen

explanation.definitionFit: A voter at an election marks the chosen candidate on the ballot with an X.

clue.text: Thick soup — food to the German

parts.note: chow is slang for food
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A thick soup is handed over as food for a German guest.
explanation.definitionFit: Chowder is a thick soup, typically of clams or fish with potatoes.

clue.text: No, no Miss Newman!

parts.note: a musical comedy title begins No, No and ends with the first name of the English actress Miss Newman

explanation.definitionFit: The actress Nanette Newman shares her first name with the heroine of the 1925 musical No, No, Nanette.

clue.text: Note golf score, adequate — may be fixed

parts.note: re is the second note of the tonic sol-fa scale
par is the standard score for a golf hole
able means competent or adequate

explanation.surface: A golfer notes an acceptable score that might be improved.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reparable can be mended, which is to say it is capable of being fixed.

clue.text: Principle of having it both ways?

indicators.note: the word reads identically forwards and backwards, so it goes either way

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A question about the principle of wanting things both ways.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'having it both ways' is reinterpreted: the answer reads the same in both directions.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a belief or doctrine held as true, a firm principle.

clue.text: Sort of broth to beat

indicators.note: sort is read as a verb, so the letters are sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: A remark that a kind of soup is to be whisked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' rearranges BROTH; 'to' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To throb is to pulse or beat rhythmically, as a heart does.

clue.text: A lone crab scuttles round by the sea in Spain

indicators.note: a crab scuttling round moves about, so its letters are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A solitary crab scurries around a Spanish beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Barcelona is a Spanish port city on the Mediterranean coast, so a place by the sea in Spain.

clue.text: Students should draw on his advice

definitions.text: Students should draw on his advice

parts.words: Students should draw on his advice
parts.note: draw on seems to mean make use of, but here the students literally draw as their teacher advises

explanation.definitionFit: An art teacher instructs pupils in drawing, so they draw following his guidance.

clue.text: Artist who has designs on his clients

definitions.text: Artist who has designs on his clients

parts.words: Artist who has designs on his clients
parts.note: having designs on someone suggests scheming, but here the designs are inked onto customers' skin

explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo artist literally puts designs on the bodies of the people who hire him.

clue.text: Shame! Don't believe it!

definitions.meaning: disgrace or loss of reputation, a noun sense
an instruction to refuse credence to a claim, the verb sense

explanation.definitionFit: Discredit is both disgrace or dishonour and, as a verb, to doubt or disbelieve something.

clue.text: Richard admits blunder with lifting equipment

indicators.note: the name for Richard lets the blunder into its middle

parts.note: Dick is a familiar form of Richard
to err is to make a mistake or blunder

explanation.surface: Richard confesses to making a mistake with some machinery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admits' is the container signal, not a confession; the surface Richard is just a familiar name to be shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: A derrick is a type of crane or framework used for hoisting heavy loads.

clue.text: A sign of a poisonous creature

definitions.text: A sign of a poisonous creature

parts.words: A sign of a poisonous creature
parts.note: seems to mean evidence of a venomous animal nearby, but means the zodiac sign named after one

explanation.definitionFit: The eighth sign of the zodiac is symbolised by the scorpion, a venomous animal.

clue.text: When it reacts saltpetre may be extracted

indicators.note: the letters are pulled out of the run of words in the clue

explanation.surface: A chemistry note on obtaining saltpetre from a reaction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be extracted' signals letters taken from inside WHEN IT REACTS; the surface sounds like laboratory chemistry.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitre is another name for saltpetre, potassium nitrate.

clue.text: Leave the road and stop

definitions.meaning: to exit a main road onto a side road
to switch off a machine or tap, halting it

explanation.definitionFit: To turn off is both to leave one road for another and to switch something off, stopping it.

clue.text: Comes into force?

parts.note: the phrase usually means takes legal effect, but here someone joins the armed forces

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who signs up for military service joins one of the armed forces.

clue.text: It flows by river edge

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
to edge a blade is to hone it, sharpening it

explanation.walkthrough: 'by' links the pieces; 'edge' is a verb meaning sharpen.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhone is a major river of Switzerland and France, so something that flows.

clue.text: Villain knocked nurse cold

indicators.note: the letters are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A villain strikes a nurse unconscious.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoundrel is a dishonest rogue, a synonym for villain.

clue.text: Time for some magic

definitions.meaning: a period, as in a ... of fine weather
a charm or incantation that works magic

explanation.definitionFit: A spell is both a stretch of time and a magical incantation.

clue.text: Dinar in trouble, at its lowest point

indicators.note: the word is troubled, stirred into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A currency in crisis, at its lowest value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' rearranges DINAR, a currency of several countries.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the bottom or worst point of something, opposite of the zenith.

clue.text: I am quietly learning to beg

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
lore is knowledge or learning

explanation.surface: Someone says they are studying quietly in order to plead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To implore someone is to beg them earnestly.

clue.text: Eating here is no picnic

parts.note: no picnic usually means hard going, but literally a meal not taken outdoors

explanation.definitionFit: A picnic is eaten out of doors, so a meal inside the house is not a picnic.

clue.text: A professor of infinite wisdom

parts.note: not an academic but someone who professes, or claims, to understand everything

explanation.definitionFit: A know-it-all claims to be wise about every subject, professing limitless knowledge.

clue.text: Menus, perhaps, thanks to Berbers

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks
the Riffs are a Berber people of the Rif mountains of Morocco

explanation.surface: A diner thanks some North African tribesmen for the bill of fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' links the pieces. TA is an everyday British word for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A tariff is a list of prices, so a menu is an example of one, hence 'perhaps'.
